memberdef.name: QLaw

parameterdescription.para: A target orbit described by Classical Orbital Elements.
The gravitational parameter of the central body.
A set of parameters for the QLaw.
The domain of the Classical Orbital Elements. Defaults to Osculating.
The strategy to compute the gradient of the QLaw. Defaults to FiniteDifference

The frame in which the orbital elements are computed and the target COE is defined. The states provided to the guidance law are converted to this frame and the resulting thrust is rotated back to the frame of the dynamics. Its Z axis defines the pole the inclination and RAAN are measured against, so a frame aligned with the true pole (e.g. CIRF or TEME) is appropriate for mean elements. Defaults to GCRF.

briefdescription.para: The Q-law is a Lyapunov feedback control law developed by Petropoulos, based on analytic expressions for maximum rates of change of the orbit elements and the desired changes in the elements. Q, the proximity quotient, serves as a candidate Lyapunov function. As the spacecraft approaches the target orbit, Q decreases monotonically (becoming zero at the target orbit). https://dataverse.jpl.nasa.gov/api/access/datafile/10307?gbrecs=true https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370849580_Analytic_Calculation_and_Application_of_the_Q-Law_Guidance_Algorithm_Partial_Derivatives https://dataverse.jpl.nasa.gov/api/access/datafile/13727?gbrecs=true.
